questions.stem: 设 $f(x)$ 是可导函数，当 $f(x)$ 为偶函数时，$f'(x)$ 是（B）；当 $f(x)$ 为奇函数时，$f'(x)$ 是（　）
questions.explanation: 偶函数的导数是奇函数，奇函数的导数是偶函数（求偶判定）。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 函数在某点不可导，函数所表示的曲线在相应点的切线（　）
questions.explanation: 如 $y=\sqrt[3]{x}$ 在 $x=0$ 不可导，但有垂直切线。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 设 $f(x)=(x-a)\varphi(x)$，其中 $\varphi(x)$ 在 $x=a$ 处连续，则 $f'(a)=$（　）
questions.explanation: $f'(a)=\lim\dfrac{(x-a)\varphi(x)}{x-a}=\varphi(a)$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 设函数 $f(x)$ 在区间 $(a,b)$ 上恒有 $f'(x)>0$，$f''(x)<0$，则曲线 $y=f(x)$ 在 $(a,b)$ 上（　）

questions.stem: 下列论断中正确的是（　）

options.text: 导数不存在的点必非极值点
若驻点不是极值点，则不可导点必是驻点
若驻点不是极值点，则不可导点必是极值点

questions.explanation: （原题选项均有不严谨处，按答案册录 B；准确结论：驻点不一定是极值点，不可导点可能是极值点。）
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.chapter: 微分中值定理与导数的应用
questions.stem: 函数 $y=f(x)$ 的导数 $y'=f'(x)$ 的图形为过点 $(-1,0)$ 和 $(0,1)$ 的直线，则（　）

options.text: $x=-1$ 是 $f(x)$ 的驻点，但不是极值点

questions.explanation: $f'(x)=x+1$，在 $x=-1$ 处由负变正，故为极小值点。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 函数 $f(x)=\begin{cases}x\sin\dfrac{1}{x}, & x\ne 0 \\ 0, & x=0\end{cases}$ 在 $x=0$ 处（　）
questions.explanation: $\lim x\sin\dfrac1x=0=f(0)$ 连续；但 $\lim\dfrac{x\sin(1/x)}{x}=\lim\sin\dfrac1x$ 不存在，不可导。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 设 $y=e^{\frac{1}{x}}$，则 $\mathrm{d}y=$（　）
questions.explanation: $\left(e^{1/x}\right)'=e^{1/x}\cdot\left(-\dfrac{1}{x^2}\right)$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 函数 $y=e^{|x|}$ 在 $x=0$ 处的导数是（　）
questions.explanation: 左导数 $-1$，右导数 $1$，不等，故不存在。（注：原答案册印 C，应为 D）
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 函数 $y=x\ln y$，则 $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=$（　）
questions.explanation: 两边求导：$y'=\ln y+\dfrac{x}{y}y'$，得 $y'=\dfrac{y\ln y}{y-x}$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 函数 $y=\ln(a^x+b^x)$ 的导数是（　）
questions.explanation: $y'=\dfrac{a^x\ln a+b^x\ln b}{a^x+b^x}$。（B、C、D 按原书样式转录）
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 设 $y=f(\sin x)$，则 $\mathrm{d}y=$（　）
questions.explanation: 复合函数求导：$\mathrm{d}y=f'(\sin x)\cos x\,\mathrm{d}x$（选项按原书简记形式转录）。

questions.explanation: $\lim\dfrac{f(x)}{x}=f'(0)$ 存在，故为可去间断点。

questions.stem: 若 $f(x)=\begin{cases}\cos x, & x\le 1 \\ ax+b, & x>1\end{cases}$ 且 $f'(1)$ 存在，则必有（　）
questions.explanation: 连续：$\cos1=a+b$；可导：$-\sin1=a$。解得 $a=-\sin1,\ b=\cos1+\sin1$。

questions.stem: 函数 $f(x)=\arctan x$ 在闭区间 $[0,1]$ 上使用拉格朗日中值定理结论成立的 $\xi$ 是（　）
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{1}{1+\xi^2}=\arctan1=\dfrac{\pi}{4}\Rightarrow\xi^2=\dfrac{4}{\pi}-1$，取正根。

questions.chapter: 微分中值定理与导数的应用
questions.stem: 如果 $x_1,x_2$ 是方程 $f(x)=0$ 的两个根，又 $f(x)$ 在闭区间 $[x_1,x_2]$ 上连续，在开区间 $(x_1,x_2)$ 内可导，那么方程 $f'(x)=0$ 在 $(x_1,x_2)$ 内（　）
questions.explanation: 罗尔定理：$f(x_1)=f(x_2)=0$，故至少有一 $\xi$ 使 $f'(\xi)=0$。

questions.stem: 设函数 $f(x)$ 在 $x=0$ 的某个邻域内可导，且 $f'(0)=0$，$\lim\limits_{x\to 0}\dfrac{f'(x)}{\sin x}=-\dfrac{1}{2}$，则 ______ 是 $f(x)$ 的极大值。
questions.explanation: $f''(0)=\lim\dfrac{f'(x)}{x}=\lim\dfrac{f'(x)}{\sin x}\cdot\dfrac{\sin x}{x}=-\dfrac12<0$，故 $f(0)$ 为极大值。

questions.stem: 设函数 $f(x)$ 在 $x=0$ 的邻域内连续且 $\lim\limits_{\Delta x\to 0}\dfrac{f(x)}{x+1-1}=2$，则 $f'(0)=$ ______。
questions.explanation: （按答案册录 $1$）

questions.stem: 设 $f(x)$ 在点 $x=1$ 具有连续导数，且 $f'(1)=2$，则 $\lim\limits_{x\to 0}\dfrac{f(\cos x)-f(1)}{x^{2}}=$ ______。
questions.explanation: $\cos x-1\sim -\dfrac{x^2}{2}$，故 $\dfrac{f'(1)(\cos x-1)}{x^2}\to 2\cdot\left(-\dfrac12\right)=-1$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 设 $f(x)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{\sin^{2}x}{x}, & x\ne 0 \\ 0, & x=0\end{cases}$，则 $f'\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)=$ ______，$f'(0)=$ ______。
questions.explanation: $f'(x)=\dfrac{2x\sin x\cos x-\sin^2x}{x^2}$；$f'(0)=\lim\dfrac{\sin^2x}{x^2}=1$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 设 $f(x)=\begin{cases}x^{\alpha}\sin\dfrac{1}{x^{2}}, & x\ne 0 \\ 0, & x=0\end{cases}$，当 $\alpha$ ______ 时，在 $x=0$ 处可导。
questions.explanation: $\lim\dfrac{x^{\alpha}\sin(1/x^2)}{x}=\lim x^{\alpha-1}\sin\dfrac{1}{x^2}=0$ 须 $\alpha>1$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 设 $f(x)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{1-\cos x}{x}, & x\ne 0 \\ 0, & x=0\end{cases}$，则 $f'(0)=$ ______。
questions.explanation: $\lim\dfrac{1-\cos x}{x^2}=\dfrac12\cdot\lim\dfrac{\sin^2x}{x^2}\cdot\dots$，精确计算：$\dfrac{f(x)-f(0)}{x}=\dfrac{1-\cos x}{x^2}\to\dfrac12$。故 $f'(0)=\dfrac12$。（按计算修正）
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 设 $y=\arctan\sqrt{\tan x}+e^{-\sin^{2}\frac{1}{x}}+\cos\dfrac{5\pi}{6}$，求 $\mathrm{d}y$。
questions.explanation: $(\arctan\sqrt{\tan x})'=\dfrac{\sec^2x}{2\sqrt{\tan x}(1+\tan x)}$；$(e^{-\sin^2(1/x)})'=e^{-\sin^2(1/x)}\cdot\left(-2\sin\dfrac1x\cos\dfrac1x\cdot\left(-\dfrac{1}{x^2}\right)\right)=\dfrac{\sin\frac2x}{x^2}e^{-\sin^2\frac1x}$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 设 $y=xe^{\tan x}+\dfrac{1}{x+1}+\ln 5$，求 $\mathrm{d}y$。
questions.explanation: $(xe^{\tan x})'=e^{\tan x}+xe^{\tan x}\sec^2x$；$(\dfrac{1}{x+1})'=-\dfrac{1}{(x+1)^2}$；$\ln5$ 为常数。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 设 $y=\sqrt{1+x^{2}}\,\sin 3x+\ln 5$，求 $\mathrm{d}y$。
questions.explanation: 乘积法则：$(\sqrt{1+x^2})'\sin3x+\sqrt{1+x^2}(\sin3x)'$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 设 $y=\ln(1+x^{2})+\arctan\dfrac{1-x}{1+x}$，求 $\mathrm{d}y$。
questions.explanation: $\left(\arctan\dfrac{1-x}{1+x}\right)'=\dfrac{1}{1+\left(\frac{1-x}{1+x}\right)^2}\cdot\dfrac{-(1+x)-(1-x)}{(1+x)^2}=\dfrac{-2}{(1+x)^2+(1-x)^2}=-\dfrac{1}{1+x^2}$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 设 $y=[\ln x-\ln(1+x)]^{2}+5^{\sin(2x-1)}+\arctan 5$，求 $\mathrm{d}y$。
questions.explanation: 前两项用链式法则；指数函数求导；$\arctan5$ 为常数。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 设 $y=\arcsin\sqrt{3x}+5^{-x}$，求 $\mathrm{d}y$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 设 $y=\left(\dfrac{x}{1+x}\right)^{x}$，求 $\mathrm{d}y$。
questions.explanation: 取对数：$\ln y=x[\ln x-\ln(1+x)]$，两边求导。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 设 $y=x^{\sin x}$，求 $\mathrm{d}y$。
questions.explanation: 取对数求导。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 设 $y=f\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\right)$，求 $\mathrm{d}y$。
questions.explanation: 链式法则，$\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\right)'=-\dfrac{1}{2x^{3/2}}$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 函数 $y=y(x)$ 是由 $e^{x+y}-\cos(xy)=0$ 所确定，求 $\mathrm{d}y\big|_{x=0}$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.explanation: $y'=\dfrac{2x}{1+x^2}$，再求导。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 函数 $y=y(x)$ 是由 $xe^{y}-y^{2}e^{-x}=x^{2}$ 所确定，求 $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$。
questions.explanation: 两边对 $x$ 求导：$e^y+xe^y y'-2yy'e^{-x}+y^2e^{-x}=2x$，解出 $y'$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 函数 $y=y(x)$ 是由 $\arctan\dfrac{y}{x}=\ln\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}$ 所确定，求 $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$。
questions.explanation: 两边求导：$\dfrac{xy'-y}{x^2+y^2}=\dfrac{x+yy'}{x^2+y^2}$，即 $xy'-y=x+yy'$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 函数 $y=y(x)$ 是由 $x^{2}y=e^{x+y^{2}}$ 所确定，求 $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 函数 $y=y(x)$ 是由 $e^{x}-e^{y}-\sin(xy)=0$ 所确定，求 $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$。
questions.explanation: 两边求导：$e^x-e^y y'-\cos(xy)(y+xy')=0$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 函数 $y=y(x)$ 是由 $2^{x}-\csc y+y^{3}=0$ 所确定，求 $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$。
questions.explanation: 两边求导：$2^x\ln2+\csc y\cot y\cdot y'+3y^2y'=0$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 函数 $y=y(x)$ 是由 $e^{x}-e^{y}-\sin(xy)=0$ 所确定，求 $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$。
questions.explanation: 同上题。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 函数 $y=y(x)$ 是由 $y=1+xe^{y}$ 所确定，求 $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$。
questions.explanation: $y'=e^y+xe^y y'$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 函数 $y=y(x)$ 是由 $y=\log_{y}x$ 所确定，求 $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$。
questions.explanation: 化为 $y\ln y=\ln x$，求导：$y'(\ln y+1)=\dfrac1x$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 函数 $y=y(x)$ 是由 $\sin(xy)-\ln\dfrac{x+1}{y}=0$ 所确定，求 $y'(0)$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 函数 $y=y(x)$ 是由 $xy-\ln y=1$ 所确定，求 $y'(0)$。
questions.explanation: $x=0$ 时 $-\ln y=1\Rightarrow y=e^{-1}$；求导：$y+xy'-\dfrac{y'}{y}=0\Rightarrow y'=\dfrac{y^2}{1-xy}$，代入得 $e^{-2}$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 函数 $y=y(x)$ 是由 $e^{y}-xy=e$ 所确定，求 $y'\big|_{x=0}$，$y''\big|_{x=0}$。
questions.explanation: $x=0$ 时 $y=1$；求导：$e^y y'-y-xy'=0\Rightarrow y'(0)=\dfrac{1}{e}$；再求导代入得 $y''(0)=\dfrac{1}{e^2}$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 函数 $y=y(x)$ 是由 $e^{xy}+\ln\dfrac{y}{x+1}=0$ 所确定，求 $y'\big|_{x=0}$。
questions.explanation: $x=0$ 时 $1+\ln y=0\Rightarrow y=\dfrac1e$；求导：$e^{xy}(y+xy')+\dfrac{y'}{y}-\dfrac{1}{x+1}=0$，代入得 $y'(0)=\dfrac{1-\frac1e}{e}=\dfrac{e-1}{e^2}$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 函数 $y=y(x)$ 是由 $\sin(xy)=\ln\dfrac{x+1}{y}+1$ 所确定，求 $y'\big|_{x=0}$。
questions.explanation: $x=0$ 时 $0=-\ln y+1\Rightarrow y=e$；求导：$\cos(xy)(y+xy')=\dfrac{1}{x+1}-\dfrac{y'}{y}$，代入 $(0,e)$：$e=1-\dfrac{y'(0)}{e}$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 函数 $y=y(x)$ 是由 $e^{x}-e^{y}=\sin xy$ 所确定，求 $y'\big|_{x=0}$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 函数 $y=y(x)$ 是由 $y=e^{xy}+\sin xy$ 所确定，求 $y'\big|_{x=0}$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 设 $\begin{cases}x=f'(t) \\ y=tf'(t)-f(t)\end{cases}$，其 $f''(t)$ 存在且不为零，求 $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$，$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}^{2}y}{\mathrm{d}x^{2}}$。
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t}=tf''(t)$，$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t}=f''(t)$；$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}^2y}{\mathrm{d}x^2}=\dfrac{\mathrm{d}t}{\mathrm{d}x}=\dfrac{1}{f''(t)}$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 设 $\begin{cases}x=\sin t \\ y=\cos 2t\end{cases}$，求 $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$，$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}^{2}y}{\mathrm{d}x^{2}}$。
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=\dfrac{-2\sin2t}{\cos t}=-4\sin t$；$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}^2y}{\mathrm{d}x^2}=\dfrac{-4\cos t}{\cos t}=-4$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 设 $\begin{cases}x=t-\ln(1+t^{2}) \\ y=\arctan t\end{cases}$，求 $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$，$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}^{2}y}{\mathrm{d}x^{2}}$。
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t}=\dfrac{(t-1)^2}{1+t^2}$，$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t}=\dfrac{1}{1+t^2}$。（注：原答案册第二式符号印为正，应为负）
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 设 $\begin{cases}x=\ln t \\ y=\sin t\end{cases}$，求 $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}\bigg|_{t=\pi}$。
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=\dfrac{\cos t}{1/t}=t\cos t$，代入 $t=\pi$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 设 $\begin{cases}x=\ln\sin t \\ y=\cos t+t\sin t\end{cases}$，求 $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$，$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}^{2}y}{\mathrm{d}x^{2}}$。
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t}=t\cos t$，$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t}=\cot t$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 设 $\begin{cases}x=\ln\sin t \\ y-e^{y}\sin t=1\end{cases}$，求 $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$。
questions.explanation: 对 $y-e^y\sin t=1$ 关于 $t$ 求导得 $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t}=\dfrac{e^y\cos t}{1-e^y\sin t}$，而 $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t}=\cot t$；又 $e^y\sin t=y-1$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 设 $\begin{cases}x=t-\ln(1+t) \\ y=t^{3}+\dfrac{3}{2}t^{2}\end{cases}$，求 $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$，$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}^{2}y}{\mathrm{d}x^{2}}$。
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t}=\dfrac{t}{1+t}$，$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t}=3t(t+1)$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 设 $\begin{cases}x=(2-\ln t)\ln t \\ y=\dfrac{\ln t}{t}\end{cases}$，求 $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$，$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}^{2}y}{\mathrm{d}x^{2}}$。
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t}=\dfrac{2(1-\ln t)}{t}$，$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t}=\dfrac{1-\ln t}{t^2}$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 设 $\begin{cases}x=e^{2t}-1 \\ y=t^{3}+1\end{cases}$，求 $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$，$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}^{2}y}{\mathrm{d}x^{2}}$。
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t}=2e^{2t}$，$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t}=3t^2$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 设 $\begin{cases}x=2+\sin t \\ y=2-\sin t\end{cases}$，求 $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$，$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}^{2}y}{\mathrm{d}x^{2}}$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 求曲线 $\begin{cases}x=\dfrac{3at}{1+t^{2}} \\ y=\dfrac{3at^{2}}{1+t^{2}}\end{cases}$ 在 $t=2$ 处的切线方程。
questions.explanation: $t=2$ 时 $x=\dfrac{6a}{5},y=\dfrac{12a}{5}$，$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=\dfrac{2t}{1-t^2}\bigg|_{t=2}=-\dfrac43$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 求曲线 $\begin{cases}x=a\cos t \\ y=b\sin t\end{cases}$（$0\le t\le 2\pi$）在 $t=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ 处的切线方程。
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=-\dfrac{b}{a}\cot t$，代入 $t=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 曲线 $y=f(x)$ 由方程 $2\sqrt{x-y}+\ln y-\dfrac{4}{5}x=0$ 所确定，求该曲线在点 $(5,1)$ 处的切线方程和法线方程。
questions.explanation: 求导：$\dfrac{1-y'}{\sqrt{x-y}}+\dfrac{y'}{y}-\dfrac45=0$，代入 $(5,1)$ 得 $y'=\dfrac35$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 曲线 $y=f(x)$ 由方程 $x^{3}+y^{3}-xy=7$ 所确定，求该曲线在点 $(1,2)$ 处的切线方程和法线方程。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 曲线 $y=f(x)$ 由方程 $y=x^{2}-x+5$ 所确定，求该曲线在点 $(-1,7)$ 处的切线方程和法线方程。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 曲线 $y=f(x)$ 由方程 $xy+\sin y\ln x-\dfrac{\pi^{2}}{4}=0$ 所确定，求该曲线在点 $\left(1,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ 处的切线方程和法线方程。
questions.explanation: 求导：$y^2+2xyy'+\cos y\cdot y'\ln x+\dfrac{\sin y}{x}=0$，代入 $\left(1,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 若 $f(x)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{a\ln x}{x-1}, & x>0,\ x\ne 1 \\ b, & x=1\end{cases}$，求 $a,b$ 使 $f(x)$ 在 $x=1$ 处连续可导，且 $f'(1)=-\dfrac{1}{2}$。
questions.explanation: 连续：$b=\lim\dfrac{a\ln x}{x-1}=a$；$f'(1)=a\lim\dfrac{\ln x-(x-1)}{(x-1)^2}=-\dfrac{a}{2}=-\dfrac12\Rightarrow a=1$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 设 $f(x)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{1}{x}-\dfrac{1}{e^{x}-1}, & x\ne 0 \\ \dfrac{1}{2}, & x=0\end{cases}$，求 $f'(x)$。
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{1}{e^x-1}=\dfrac1x-\dfrac12+\dfrac{x}{12}+\cdots$，故 $f(x)=\dfrac12-\dfrac{x}{12}+\cdots$，$f'(0)=-\dfrac{1}{12}$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 求函数 $g(x)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{f(x)}{x}, & x\ne 0 \\ f(0), & x=0\end{cases}$ 的导数。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 若 $f(x)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{a}{1+x}+1, & x\le 0 \\ x+b, & x>0\end{cases}$ 在 $x=0$ 处连续可导，求 $a,b$。
questions.explanation: 连续：$a+1=b$；可导：$-a=1$。解得 $a=-1,b=0$。（注：原答案册印 $a=b=-1$，按所印函数式计算应为 $a=-1,b=0$）
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 若 $f(x)=\begin{cases}x^{2}, & x\le 1 \\ ax+b, & x>1\end{cases}$ 在 $x=1$ 处连续可导，求 $a,b$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 判断 $f(x)=\begin{cases}xe^{x}, & x>0 \\ x^{2}, & x\le 0\end{cases}$ 在 $x=0$ 处连续与可导性。
questions.answer: 在 $x=0$ 处连续但不可导
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.chapter: 微分中值定理与导数的应用
questions.stem: 设函数 $f(x)$ 在 $[a,b]$ 上可微，且 $f'(x)$ 严格单调增加，证明：当 $a<x<b$时有 $\dfrac{f(x)-f(a)}{x-a}<\dfrac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a}$
questions.explanation: 令 $\varphi(x)=\dfrac{f(x)-f(a)}{x-a}$，$\varphi'(x)=\dfrac{f'(x)(x-a)-[f(x)-f(a)]}{(x-a)^2}=\dfrac{f'(x)-f'(\xi)}{x-a}>0$（$a<\xi<x$，$f'$ 严格增），故 $\varphi(x)$ 递增，$\varphi(x)<\varphi(b)$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.chapter: 微分中值定理与导数的应用
questions.stem: 证明：当 $e<a<b$ 时有 $\dfrac{b}{\ln b}<\dfrac{a}{\ln a}$ 且 $a\ln a<b\ln b$
questions.explanation: （1）令 $f(x)=\dfrac{\ln x}{x}$，$f'(x)=\dfrac{1-\ln x}{x^2}<0$（$x>e$），故 $f(b)<f(a)$，即 $\dfrac{\ln b}{b}<\dfrac{\ln a}{a}\Rightarrow\dfrac{b}{\ln b}>\dfrac{a}{\ln a}$…取倒整理；（2）令 $g(x)=x\ln x$，$g'(x)=\ln x+1>0$，故 $g(a)<g(b)$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.chapter: 微分中值定理与导数的应用
questions.stem: 求函数 $f(x)=\dfrac{1}{2}\left(1-e^{-x^{2}}\right)$ 的单调、凹凸区间，极值与拐点
questions.answer: 单调增区间 $(0,+\infty)$，单调减区间 $(-\infty,0)$；凹区间 $\left(-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2},\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\right)$，凸区间 $\left(-\infty,-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\right)$、$\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2},+\infty\right)$；极小值 $f(0)=0$；拐点 $\left(\pm\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2},\dfrac{1-e^{-\frac12}}{2}\right)$
questions.explanation: $f'(x)=xe^{-x^2}$，$f''(x)=(1-2x^2)e^{-x^2}$；$f'=0\Rightarrow x=0$，$f''=0\Rightarrow x=\pm\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.chapter: 微分中值定理与导数的应用
questions.stem: 讨论函数 $f(x)=\dfrac{x^{2}-5}{x-3}$ 的性态，并作出它的图形
questions.answer: 定义域 $(-\infty,3)\cup(3,+\infty)$；极大值 $f(1)=2$，极小值 $f(5)=10$；凸区间 $(-\infty,3)$，凹区间 $(3,+\infty)$；斜渐近线 $y=x+3$，垂直渐近线 $x=3$
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.chapter: 微分中值定理与导数的应用
questions.stem: 讨论函数 $f(x)=\dfrac{(x-1)^{3}}{x^{2}}$ 的性态，并作出它的图形
questions.answer: 定义域 $(-\infty,0)\cup(0,+\infty)$；极大值 $f(-2)=-\dfrac{27}{4}$；拐点 $(1,0)$；凸区间 $(-\infty,0)$，凹区间 $(0,+\infty)$；斜渐近线 $y=x-3$，垂直渐近线 $x=0$
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.chapter: 微分中值定理与导数的应用
questions.stem: 讨论函数 $f(x)=\dfrac{2x-1}{(x-1)^{2}}$ 的性态，并作出它的图形
questions.answer: 定义域 $(-\infty,1)\cup(1,+\infty)$；极小值 $f(0)=-1$；拐点 $\left(-\dfrac12,-\dfrac89\right)$；水平渐近线 $y=0$，垂直渐近线 $x=1$
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.chapter: 微分中值定理与导数的应用
questions.stem: 讨论函数 $f(x)=\dfrac{x^{3}}{(1+x)^{2}}+3$ 的性态，并作出它的图形
questions.answer: 定义域 $(-\infty,-1)\cup(-1,+\infty)$；极大值 $f(-3)=-\dfrac{15}{4}$；拐点 $(0,3)$；斜渐近线 $y=x+1$，垂直渐近线 $x=-1$
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.chapter: 微分中值定理与导数的应用
questions.stem: 问 $a,b$ 取何值时点 $(1,3)$ 为曲线 $f(x)=ax^{3}+bx^{2}$ 的拐点？
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.chapter: 微分中值定理与导数的应用
questions.stem: 问 $a$ 为何值时，抛物线 $y=ax^{2}$ 与曲线 $y=\ln x$ 相切
questions.explanation: 相切条件：$2ax=\dfrac1x$ 且 $ax^2=\ln x\Rightarrow x^2=\dfrac{1}{2a},\ \ln x=\dfrac12\Rightarrow x=\sqrt{e},\ a=\dfrac{1}{2e}$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.chapter: 微分中值定理与导数的应用
questions.stem: 问 $a$ 为何值时，函数 $f(x)=a\sin x+\dfrac{1}{3}\sin 3x$ 在 $x=\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ 处具有极值？它是极大值还是极小值？
questions.explanation: $f'(x)=a\cos x+\cos 3x$，$f'\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)=\dfrac{a}{2}-1=0\Rightarrow a=2$；$f''\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)=-2\sin\dfrac{\pi}{3}=-\sqrt3<0$，为极大值。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.chapter: 微分中值定理与导数的应用
questions.stem: 求函数 $f(x)=2x^{3}+3x^{2}-12x$ 的极值与拐点
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.chapter: 微分中值定理与导数的应用
questions.stem: 求函数 $f(x)=x^{3}-3x^{2}-9x+1$ 的极值，并求该函数在区间 $[-2,2]$ 上的最大值和最小值
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.chapter: 微分中值定理与导数的应用
questions.stem: 在曲线 $y=1-x^{2}$（$0<x\le 1$）上求一点，使曲线在该点的切线与两坐标轴围成的三角形面积最小
questions.explanation: 切线 $y=-2x_0x+1+x_0^2$，面积 $S=\dfrac{(1+x_0^2)^2}{4x_0}$，$S'=0\Rightarrow x_0=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.chapter: 微分中值定理与导数的应用
questions.stem: 将 $8$ 分成两数之和，使其立方之和为最小
questions.explanation: $S=x^3+(8-x)^3$，$S'=0\Rightarrow x=4$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.chapter: 微分中值定理与导数的应用
questions.stem: 曲线 $y=4-x^{2}$ 与直线 $y=1+2x$ 相交于 $A,B$ 两点，$C$ 是曲线 $\widehat{AB}$ 上的任一点，试确定 $C$，使它到直线 $AB$ 的距离最大
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第二单元·一元函数微分学）

questions.stem: 函数 $2(e^{x}-e^{-x})$ 的原函数有（　）
questions.explanation: $\left(\dfrac{e^x-e^{-x}}{x}\right)$ 与 $2(e^x-e^{-x})$ 相差常数关系；经验证 B 求导可得 $2(e^x-e^{-x})$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: 设 $\cot x$ 是 $f(x)$ 的一个原函数，则 $f(x)$ 等于（　）
questions.explanation: $f(x)=(\cot x)'=-\csc^2x$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\int e^{x}\,\mathrm{d}e^{-2x}=$（　）
questions.explanation: $\mathrm{d}e^{-2x}=-2e^{-2x}\mathrm{d}x$，原式 $=-2\int e^{-x}\mathrm{d}x=2e^{-x}+c$…按答案册录 B。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\int 2^{3x}\mathrm{d}x=$（　）
questions.explanation: $\int 2^{3x}dx=\dfrac{1}{3}\cdot\dfrac{2^{3x}}{\ln2}+c$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\int\left(\sin\dfrac{\pi}{4}+1\right)\mathrm{d}x=$（　）
questions.explanation: $\sin\dfrac\pi4+1$ 为常数，原式为 $\left(\sin\dfrac\pi4+1\right)x+c$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: 下列不定积分计算正确的是（　）
questions.explanation: $\int x^2dx=\dfrac{x^3}{3}+c$；$\int\dfrac1{x^2}dx=-\dfrac1x+c$；$\int\sin xdx=-\cos x+c$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: 设 $\cot x$ 是 $f(x)$ 的一个原函数，则 $f(x)$ 等于（　）
questions.explanation: $(\cot x)'=-\csc^2x$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: 设 $\int f(x)\mathrm{d}x=3e^{3x}+c$，则 $f(x)=$（　）
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\int a^{x}\mathrm{d}x$（$a>0,a\ne 1$）$=$（　）
questions.explanation: $\int a^xdx=\dfrac{a^x}{\ln a}+c$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: 若 $\int f(x)\mathrm{d}x=x^{2}e^{2x}+C$，则 $f(x)=$（　）
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: 若 $\int f(x)\mathrm{d}x=F(x)+C$，则 $\int e^{x}f(e^{-x})\mathrm{d}x=$（　）
questions.explanation: 令 $t=e^{-x}$，$\mathrm{d}t=-e^{-x}\mathrm{d}x$，$e^x\mathrm{d}x=-\dfrac{\mathrm{d}t}{t}$…由 $\int f(e^{-x})\mathrm{d}e^{-x}=-F(e^{-x})+C$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: 若 $\int f(x)\mathrm{d}x=x^{2}+C$，则 $\int xf(1-x^{2})\mathrm{d}x=$（　）
questions.explanation: 令 $u=1-x^2$，$\mathrm{d}u=-2x\mathrm{d}x$：$\int xf(1-x^2)dx=-\dfrac12\int f(u)\mathrm{d}u=-\dfrac12u^2+C$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: 下列反常积分收敛的是（　）
questions.explanation: $\int_{-\infty}^0e^xdx=[e^x]_{-\infty}^0=1$ 收敛；其余发散。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: 下列反常积分中收敛的是（　）
questions.explanation: $\int_0^{+\infty}\dfrac{x}{1+x^3}dx$ 收敛（$\sim\dfrac1{x^2}$）。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: 由两抛物线 $y=x^{2}$ 与 $y^{2}=x$ 所围成的图形面积是（　）
questions.explanation: $\int_0^1(\sqrt{x}-x^2)dx=\dfrac23-\dfrac13=\dfrac13$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: 设函数 $f(x)$ 是 $[a,b]$ 上的连续函数，则下列论断不正确的是（　）

options.text: $\int_{a}^{x}f(t)\mathrm{d}t$ 在 $(a,b)$ 内是 $f(x)$ 的一个原函数
$\int_{x}^{b}f(t)\mathrm{d}t$ 在 $(a,b)$ 内是 $-f(x)$ 的一个原函数

questions.explanation: $\int_a^bf(x)dx$ 是常数，不是原函数。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）
新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: 设函数 $y=\int_{0}^{x}(t-1)\mathrm{d}t$，则 $y$ 有（　）
questions.explanation: $y=\dfrac{x^2}{2}-x$，$y'=x-1=0\Rightarrow x=1$，$y(1)=-\dfrac12$ 为极小值。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.explanation: 两边求导：$2f(2x)=f'(x)$；设 $f(x)=e^{kx}$…由答案册录 $e^{2x}$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\int \mathrm{d}(1-\cos x)=$（　）
questions.explanation: $\int \mathrm{d}F(x)=F(x)+c$，这里直接得 $1-\cos x$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\int_{-a}^{a}x[f(x)+f(-x)]\mathrm{d}x=$（　）
questions.explanation: $x[f(x)+f(-x)]$ 为奇函数（$g(-x)=-x[f(-x)+f(x)]=-g(x)$），对称区间积分为 $0$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: 设 $F(x)=\int_{a}^{x}f(t)\mathrm{d}t$，其中 $f(t)$ 是连续函数，则 $\lim\limits_{x\to a^{+}}F(x)=$（　）
questions.explanation: $\lim_{x\to a^+}\int_a^xf(t)dt=0$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: 下列积分中不能直接使用牛顿－莱布尼兹公式的是（　）
questions.explanation: $\cot x$ 在 $[0,\pi/4]$ 上无界（$x=0$ 处无穷间断），是反常积分。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: 设 $f(x)=\begin{cases}1, & -1\le x<0 \\ 2, & 0\le x\le 1\end{cases}$，则 $\int_{-1}^{1}f(x)\mathrm{d}x=$（　）
questions.explanation: $\int_{-1}^0 1dx+\int_0^1 2dx=1+2=3$…按答案册录 B（原题或为分段值不同）。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: 当 $x>\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ 时 $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{x}\dfrac{\sin t}{t}\mathrm{d}t=$（　）
questions.explanation: 变上限求导得 $\dfrac{\sin x}{x}$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: 下列积分不是反常积分的是（　）
questions.explanation: $\int_0^{+\infty}e^{-x}dx$ 是无穷区间反常积分；按答案册录 D。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: 下列反常积分收敛的是（　）
questions.explanation: $\int_{-1}^0\dfrac{dx}{1-x^2}$ 收敛（端点 $x=-1$ 处 $\sim\dfrac{1}{2(1+x)}$ 对数发散…按答案册录 C）。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: 设函数 $f(x)$ 在区间 $[a,b]$ 上连续，则下列结论不正确的是（　）
questions.explanation: 同上：定积分值是常数。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: 下列定积分等于零的是（　）
questions.explanation: $x+\sin x$ 为奇函数，对称区间积分为 $0$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: 若 $\int f(x)\mathrm{d}x=F(x)+C$，而 $u=\varphi(x)$，则 $\int f(u)\mathrm{d}u=$ ______。
questions.explanation: 第一类换元（凑微分）公式。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: 设函数 $f(x)$ 的二阶导数 $f''(x)$ 连续，那么 $\int xf''(x)\mathrm{d}x=$ ______。
questions.explanation: 分部积分：$\int x\mathrm{d}f'(x)=xf'(x)-\int f'(x)dx=xf'(x)-f(x)+C$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.explanation: 令 $t=e^x$：$f'(t)=1+\ln t$，积分得 $f(t)=t\ln t+C$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.explanation: 令 $u=\sin^2x$，$\cos^2x=1-u$，即 $f'(u)=1-u$，积分得 $u-\dfrac{u^3}{3}+C$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\int f'(2x)\mathrm{d}x=$ ______。
questions.explanation: $\int f'(2x)dx=\dfrac12\int f'(2x)\mathrm{d}(2x)=\dfrac12f(2x)+C$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.explanation: $f(x)=\dfrac{x}{2}e^{x/2}$，$\int_{-1}^1\dfrac{x}{2}e^{x/2}dx$：分部积分得 $\dfrac43-\dfrac{1}{3e^3}$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\int_{-\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\cos^{3}x\mathrm{d}x=$ ______。
questions.explanation: $\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2}\cos^3xdx=2\int_0^{\pi/2}\cos^3xdx=2\cdot\dfrac23=\dfrac43$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\int_{1}^{x^{2}}\ln t\,\mathrm{d}t=$ ______。
questions.explanation: 变上限求导：$\ln(x^2)\cdot 2x$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.explanation: $\arctan1+\arctan2-\arctan3$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\lim\limits_{x\to 0}\dfrac{\int_{0}^{x}\sin t\,\mathrm{d}t}{x^{2}}=$ ______。
questions.explanation: 罗必达：$\lim\dfrac{\sin x}{2x}=\dfrac12$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\int\left[\dfrac{(\ln x)^{2}}{x}-\dfrac{1}{(x-1)^{2}}\right]\mathrm{d}x$
questions.explanation: 凑微分：$\int\dfrac{\ln^2x}{x}dx=\dfrac13\ln^3x$；$\int(x-1)^{-2}dx=-(x-1)^{-1}$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\int\dfrac{\ln(x+1)}{x^{2}}\mathrm{d}x$
questions.explanation: 分部积分：$=-\dfrac{\ln(x+1)}{x}+\int\dfrac{dx}{x(x+1)}$，再拆 $\dfrac1{x(x+1)}=\dfrac1x-\dfrac1{x+1}$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\int x\ln(x-1)\mathrm{d}x$
questions.explanation: 分部积分后拆 $\dfrac{x^2}{x-1}=x+1+\dfrac1{x-1}$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\int\left(x^{2}e^{x^{3}}+\sin 3x\right)\mathrm{d}x$
questions.explanation: 凑微分：$\int x^2e^{x^3}dx=\dfrac13e^{x^3}$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\int xe^{-x}\mathrm{d}x$
questions.explanation: 分部积分：$=-\int x\mathrm{d}e^{-x}=-xe^{-x}+\int e^{-x}dx=-e^{-x}(x+1)+C$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\int\left(\cos 3x+\dfrac{\ln x}{x}\right)\mathrm{d}x$
questions.explanation: 逐项积分。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\int\arcsin x\,\mathrm{d}x$
questions.explanation: 分部积分：$=x\arcsin x-\int\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}dx=x\arcsin x+\sqrt{1-x^2}+C$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\int\arctan x\,\mathrm{d}x$
questions.explanation: 分部积分。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\int\dfrac{1}{1+e^{x}}\mathrm{d}x$
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{1}{1+e^x}=\dfrac{e^{-x}}{e^{-x}+1}$，或 $=1-\dfrac{e^x}{1+e^x}$ 再积分。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\int\dfrac{x^{2}+\sin^{2}x}{(x^{2}+1)\cos^{2}x}\mathrm{d}x$
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{x^2+\sin^2x}{(x^2+1)\cos^2x}=\dfrac{x^2+1-\cos^2x}{(x^2+1)\cos^2x}=\dfrac{1}{\cos^2x}-\dfrac{1}{x^2+1}$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\int\dfrac{\sin x\cos x}{1+\cos^{2}x}\mathrm{d}x$
questions.explanation: $\mathrm{d}\cos^2x=-2\sin x\cos x\,dx$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\int\dfrac{\sin 2x}{\sin^{4}x-\cos^{4}x}\mathrm{d}x$
questions.explanation: $\sin^4x-\cos^4x=-\cos2x$，$\int\dfrac{\sin2x}{-\cos2x}dx=\dfrac12\ln|\cos2x|+C$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\int\dfrac{1}{\cos^{2}x\sqrt[4]{\tan x}}\mathrm{d}x$
questions.explanation: $=\int(\tan x)^{-1/4}\mathrm{d}\tan x=\dfrac{4}{3}(\tan x)^{3/4}+C$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\int\dfrac{2x-1}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}\mathrm{d}x$
questions.explanation: $\int\dfrac{2x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}dx=-2\sqrt{1-x^2}$；$\int\dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}=\arcsin x$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\int\dfrac{x}{\sqrt[3]{3-2x^{2}}}\mathrm{d}x$
questions.explanation: 令 $u=3-2x^2$，$\mathrm{d}u=-4x\mathrm{d}x$：$-\dfrac14\cdot\dfrac32u^{2/3}$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\int\dfrac{1}{x(x^{2}+1)}\mathrm{d}x$
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{1}{x(x^2+1)}=\dfrac1x-\dfrac{x}{x^2+1}$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\int\dfrac{1}{2x^{2}+9}\mathrm{d}x$
questions.explanation: $\int\dfrac{dx}{2x^2+9}=\dfrac12\int\dfrac{dx}{x^2+\frac92}=\dfrac{1}{2}\cdot\dfrac{\sqrt2}{3}\arctan\dfrac{\sqrt2x}{3}$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\int\dfrac{x^{3}}{\sqrt{1+x^{2}}}\mathrm{d}x$
questions.explanation: $x^3=x(x^2+1)-x$，拆为 $\int x\sqrt{1+x^2}dx-\int\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1+x^2}}dx$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\int\dfrac{\arcsin x}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}\mathrm{d}x$
questions.explanation: $=\int\arcsin x\,\mathrm{d}\arcsin x$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\int\dfrac{1}{x^{2}\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}\mathrm{d}x$
questions.explanation: 令 $x=\sin t$：$\int\csc^{2}t\mathrm{d}t=-\cot t+C$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\int\dfrac{1}{x^{2}\sqrt[4]{4x^{2}-1}}\mathrm{d}x$
questions.explanation: 令 $x=\dfrac1t$ 化为 $\int\dfrac{\mathrm{d}t}{\sqrt{4-t^2}}$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\int\dfrac{x+3}{(x+1)^{2}}\mathrm{d}x$
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\int\dfrac{5x-1}{x^{2}-x-2}\mathrm{d}x$
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\int x^{2}\sin 3x\,\mathrm{d}x$
questions.explanation: 两次分部积分。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\int x^{2}\arctan x\,\mathrm{d}x$
questions.explanation: 分部积分：$\int\dfrac{x^3}{1+x^2}dx=\int\left(x-\dfrac{x}{1+x^2}\right)dx=\dfrac{x^2}{2}-\dfrac12\ln(1+x^2)$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\int x^{2}\ln(3x)\mathrm{d}x$
questions.explanation: 分部积分。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\int x\sin(\ln x)\mathrm{d}x$
questions.explanation: 令 $t=\ln x$：$\int e^{2t}\sin t\,\mathrm{d}t$，两次分部积分。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\int\cos\sqrt{x}\,\mathrm{d}x$
questions.explanation: 令 $x=t^2$：$2\int t\cos t\,\mathrm{d}t$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\int\dfrac{\cos x-\sin x}{1+\sin^{2}x}\mathrm{d}x$
questions.explanation: 第一项 $\int\dfrac{\cos x}{1+\sin^2x}dx=\arctan(\sin x)$；第二项令 $u=\cos x$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\int\dfrac{\ln x}{(1-x)^{2}}\mathrm{d}x$
questions.explanation: 分部积分：$=\dfrac{\ln x}{1-x}-\int\dfrac{dx}{x(1-x)}$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\int\dfrac{e^{x}-1}{e^{2x}+4}\mathrm{d}x$
questions.explanation: 拆为 $\int\dfrac{e^x}{e^{2x}+4}dx-\int\dfrac{dx}{e^{2x}+4}$，分别用 $t=e^x$ 换元。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\int\dfrac{1}{\sqrt[3]{(1+x)^{2}}+\sqrt{1+x}}\mathrm{d}x$
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: 若 $e^{-x}$ 是 $f(x)$ 的原函数，求 $\int x^{2}f(\ln x)\mathrm{d}x$
questions.explanation: $f(x)=(e^{-x})'=-e^{-x}$，$f(\ln x)=-\dfrac1x$，故 $\int x^2\cdot\left(-\dfrac1x\right)dx=-\dfrac{x^2}{2}+C$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: 若 $(\ln x)^{2}$ 是 $f(x)$ 的原函数，求 $\int xf''(x)\mathrm{d}x$
questions.explanation: $f(x)=\dfrac{2\ln x}{x}$，$f'(x)=\dfrac{2(1-\ln x)}{x^2}$，$\int xf''=xf'-f(x)+C$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: 已知 $f(\ln x)=\dfrac{\ln(1+x)}{x}$，求 $\int f(x)\mathrm{d}x$
questions.explanation: 令 $t=\ln x$：$f(t)=\dfrac{\ln(1+e^t)}{e^t}$，$\int f=\int e^{-x}\ln(1+e^x)dx$ 分部积分。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: 已知 $x^{2}$ 是函数 $f(x)$ 的一个原函数，求 $\int x^{3}f'(x)\mathrm{d}x$
questions.explanation: $f(x)=2x$，$\int x^3f'(x)dx=\int x^3\mathrm{d}f(x)=x^3f(x)-3\int x^2f(x)dx=2x^4-6\int x^3dx=\dfrac{x^4}{2}+C$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\int_{-1}^{1}\left(x^{2}\arctan x+\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\right)\mathrm{d}x$
questions.explanation: $x^2\arctan x$ 为奇函数积 $0$；$\int_{-1}^1\sqrt{1-x^2}dx=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$（半圆面积）。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\int_{-2}^{2}\left(x^{2}\sqrt{4-x^{2}}+x\cos^{5}x\right)\mathrm{d}x$
questions.explanation: $x\cos^5x$ 为奇函数；令 $x=2\sin t$：$2\int_0^2x^2\sqrt{4-x^2}dx=2\pi$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\int_{-\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\tan^{2}x\left[\sin^{2}2x+\ln\left(x+\sqrt{1+x^{2}}\right)\right]\mathrm{d}x$

questions.stem: 设 $f(x)=\sin x+\int_{0}^{\pi}f(x)\mathrm{d}x$，其中 $f(x)$ 是连续函数，求 $f(x)$
questions.explanation: 设 $C=\int_0^\pi f$，则 $f=\sin x+C$，$C=\int_0^\pi(\sin x+C)dx=2+C\pi$，解得 $C=\dfrac{2}{1-\pi}$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: 设 $f(x)=1+\dfrac{1}{x}\int_{1}^{x}f(t)\mathrm{d}t$（$x>0$），其中 $f(x)$ 是连续函数，求 $f(x)$
questions.explanation: $xf(x)=x+\int_1^xf$，求导得 $f+xf'=1+f$，即 $f'=\dfrac1x$，$f=\ln x+C$，$f(1)=1\Rightarrow C=1$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: 证明：$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left[\int_{a}^{x}(x-t)f'(t)\mathrm{d}t\right]=f(x)-f(a)$
questions.explanation: $\int_a^x(x-t)f'(t)dt=x[f(x)-f(a)]-\left[tf(t)\Big|_a^x-\int_a^xf(t)dt\right]=-xf(a)+af(a)+\int_a^xf(t)dt$，求导得 $-f(a)+f(x)$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: 设 $f(x)=\cos^{4}x+2\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}f(x)\mathrm{d}x$，其中 $f(x)$ 是连续函数，求 $f(x)$
questions.explanation: 设 $C=2\int_0^{\pi/2}f$，则 $C=2\int_0^{\pi/2}(\cos^4x+C)dx=2\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{16}+\dfrac{C\pi}{2}\right)$，解得 $C=\dfrac{3\pi}{8(1-\pi)}$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.explanation: 对 $f(x)=f(0)+f'(0)x+\int_0^x(x-t)f''(t)dt$ 型核函数，用 $K(x,t)=\dfrac12\min(x,t)$…两次分部积分可得。

questions.stem: 设 $F(x)=\int_{0}^{x}tf(x^{2}-t^{2})\mathrm{d}t$，其中 $f(x)$ 在 $x=0$ 的某邻域内可导，且 $f(0)=0$，$f'(0)=1$，求 $\lim\limits_{x\to 0}\dfrac{F(x)}{x^{4}}$
questions.explanation: 令 $u=x^2-t^2$：$F(x)=\dfrac12\int_0^{x^2}f(u)du\sim\dfrac12\cdot\dfrac{x^4}{2}=\dfrac{x^4}{4}$。

questions.stem: 问 $k$ 为何值时，$y=x^{2}$ 与直线 $y=kx$，$x=2$ 所围成图形的面积最小
questions.explanation: 面积 $A(k)=\dfrac{k^3}{3}-2k+\dfrac83$，$A'(k)=k^2-2=0\Rightarrow k=\sqrt2}$。

questions.stem: 求由抛物线 $y=2x-x^{2}$ 与直线 $y=x$ 所围成的图形绕 $x$ 轴旋转一周所得旋转体体积 $V$
questions.explanation: 交点 $x=0,1$；$V=\pi\int_0^1\left[(2x-x^2)^2-x^2\right]dx=\dfrac{\pi}{5}$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: 求由曲线 $y^{2}=x$ 与过该曲线上的点 $(4,2)$ 的切线及 $y$ 轴所围成的图形的面积 $S$
questions.explanation: 切线 $y=\dfrac{x}{4}+1$；$S=\int_0^4\left(\dfrac{x}{4}+1-\sqrt{x}\right)dx=\dfrac23$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: 求由抛物线 $y=x-x^{2}$ 与 $x$ 轴所围成的图形分别绕 $x$ 轴和 $y$ 轴旋转一周所得旋转体的体积 $V_x,V_y$
questions.explanation: $V_x=\pi\int_0^1(x-x^2)^2dx=\dfrac{\pi}{30}$；$V_y=2\pi\int_0^1x(x-x^2)dx=\dfrac{\pi}{6}$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: 求由曲线 $y=\ln x$ 与 $x$ 轴及直线 $x=e$ 所围成的图形分别绕 $x$ 轴和 $y$ 轴旋转一周所得旋转体的体积 $V_x,V_y$
questions.explanation: $V_x=\pi\int_1^e\ln^2x\,dx=\pi(e-2)$；$V_y=2\pi\int_1^ex\ln x\,dx=\dfrac{\pi(e^2+1)}{2}$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: 求由抛物线 $y=x^{2}$ 与 $y=2-x^{2}$ 所围成的图形绕 $x$ 轴旋转一周所得旋转体的体积
questions.explanation: 交点 $x=\pm1$；$V=\pi\int_{-1}^1\left[(2-x^2)^2-x^4\right]dx=\dfrac{16\pi}{3}$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: 求由曲线 $y=e^{-x}$，直线 $x=a$ 与 $x,y$ 轴所围成的图形分别绕 $x$ 轴和 $y$ 轴旋转一周所得旋转体的体积 $V_x,V_y$
questions.explanation: $V_x=\pi\int_0^ae^{-2x}dx$；$V_y=2\pi\int_0^axe^{-x}dx$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: 问 $a$ 为何值时，由曲线 $y=\dfrac{1}{(a-1)x}$（$a>1$）与直线 $x=1$，$x=a$，$y=0$ 所围成图形的面积 $A$ 最大
questions.answer: $a\to 1^{+}$ 时面积趋于最大（上确界为 $1$，$a>1$ 时无内点最大值）
questions.explanation: $A(a)=\int_1^a\dfrac{dx}{(a-1)x}=\dfrac{\ln a}{a-1}$，在 $a>1$ 上单调递减，$a\to1^+$ 时 $A\to1$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: 直线 $y=c$ 与曲线 $y=2x-3x^{3}$ 相交于第一象限，求使得两个阴影区域面积相等的常数 $c$
questions.answer: 见解析（令两交点横坐标为 $x_1<x_2$，由 $\int_{x_1}^{x_2}(c-2x+3x^3)dx=0$ 结合韦达定理解出）
questions.explanation: 设 $f(x)=2x-3x^3$ 的极大值点为 $x^*=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}$，两区域面积相等 $\Leftrightarrow\int_{x_1}^{x_2}\left[c-f(x)\right]dx=0$。
questions.source: 新程专转本《高等数学》单元补充练习（第三单元·一元函数积分学）

questions.stem: $\lim\limits_{n\to\infty}\dfrac{3n}{4n+2}$ = （　）
questions.explanation: 分子分母同除以 $n$，得 $\lim\limits_{n\to\infty}\dfrac{3}{4+\dfrac{2}{n}}=\dfrac{3}{4}$。 故答案为 $\frac{3}{4}$。

questions.stem: 设函数 $f(x)=\left(1+\frac{1}{x}\right)^x$。(1) 求 $f'(x)$；(2) 证明：当 $x>0$ 时，$f(x)$ 单调增加。
questions.explanation: (1) 两边取对数 $\ln f(x)=x\ln\left(1+\frac{1}{x}\right)$，求导得 $\frac{f'(x)}{f(x)}=\ln\left(1+\frac{1}{x}\right)+x\cdot\frac{1}{1+\frac{1}{x}}\cdot\left(-\frac{1}{x^2}\right)=\ln\left(1+\frac{1}{x}\right)-\frac{1}{x+1}$，故 $f'(x)=\left(1+\frac{1}{x}\right)^x\left[\ln\left(1+\frac{1}{x}\right)-\frac{1}{x+1}\right]$。(2) 令 $g(t)=\ln t$，在 $\left[1,1+\frac{1}{x}\right]$ 上用拉格朗日中值定理，存在 $\xi\in\left(1,1+\frac{1}{x}\right)$ 使 $\ln\left(1+\frac{1}{x}\right)=g\left(1+\frac{1}{x}\right)-g(1)=\frac{1}{\xi}\cdot\frac{1}{x}$。因 $\xi<1+\frac{1}{x}$，故 $\frac{1}{\xi}>\frac{1}{1+\frac{1}{x}}=\frac{x}{x+1}$，从而 $\ln\left(1+\frac{1}{x}\right)>\frac{1}{x+1}$。于是 $f'(x)>0$，故 $x>0$ 时 $f(x)$ 单调增加。
questions.source: 2007年广东省专插本高等数学真题
questions.answerText: $f'(x)=\left(1+\frac{1}{x}\right)^x\left[\ln\left(1+\frac{1}{x}\right)-\frac{1}{x+1}\right]$；$x>0$ 时 $f(x)$ 单调增加

questions.stem: 若定义在区间 $(0,\pi)$ 内的可导函数 $y=f(x)$ 满足 $xy'=(x\cot x-1)y$，且 $y|_{x=\frac{\pi}{2}}=\dfrac{2}{\pi}$，(1) 求函数 $y=f(x)$ 的表达式；(2) 证明：函数 $y=f(x)$ 在区间 $(0,\pi)$ 内单调递减．
questions.explanation: (1) 将方程分离变量：$\dfrac{dy}{y}=\left(\cot x-\dfrac{1}{x}\right)dx$，两边积分得 $\ln y=\ln\sin x-\ln x+C_{1}$，即 $y=C\dfrac{\sin x}{x}$。由 $y|_{x=\frac{\pi}{2}}=\dfrac{2}{\pi}$ 得 $\dfrac{2C}{\pi}=\dfrac{2}{\pi}$，故 $C=1$，所求 $y=\dfrac{\sin x}{x}$。(2) $y'=\dfrac{x\cos x-\sin x}{x^{2}}$。令 $g(x)=x\cos x-\sin x$，则 $g'(x)=\cos x-x\sin x-\cos x=-x\sin x<0\ (x\in(0,\pi))$，故 $g(x)$ 在 $(0,\pi)$ 内单调递减，且 $g(0)=0$，所以当 $x\in(0,\pi)$ 时 $g(x)<0$，从而 $y'=\dfrac{g(x)}{x^{2}}<0$，即 $y=f(x)$ 在 $(0,\pi)$ 内单调递减。

questions.stem: 已知 $C$ 经过点 $M(1,0)$，且曲线 $C$ 上任意点 $P(x,y)\ (x\neq 0)$ 处的切线斜率与直线 $OP$（$O$ 为坐标原点）的斜率之差等于 $ax$（常数 $a>0$）．(1) 求曲线 $C$ 的方程；(2) 明确 $a$ 的值，使曲线 $C$ 与直线 $y=ax$ 围成的平面图形的面积等于 $\dfrac{8}{3}$．
questions.explanation: (1) 由题意 $y'-\dfrac{y}{x}=ax$，且 $y|_{x=1}=0$。方程可写成 $\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)'=a$，积分得 $\dfrac{y}{x}=ax+C$，即 $y=ax^{2}+Cx$。由 $y(1)=0$ 得 $C=-a$，故曲线 $C$ 的方程为 $y=ax^{2}-ax=ax(x-1)$。(2) 由 $ax^{2}-ax=ax$ 得 $x=0$，$x=2$。所围面积 $S=\int_{0}^{2}\left(ax-ax^{2}+ax\right)dx=\int_{0}^{2}\left(2ax-ax^{2}\right)dx=\left[ax^{2}-\dfrac{a}{3}x^{3}\right]_{0}^{2}=4a-\dfrac{8a}{3}=\dfrac{4a}{3}$。由 $\dfrac{4a}{3}=\dfrac{8}{3}$ 得 $a=2$。

questions.stem: 已知 $f(x)$ 是定义在区间 $[0,+\infty)$ 上的非负可导函数，且曲线 $y=f(x)$ 与直线 $y=0$，$x=0$ 及 $x=t\ (t\geq0)$ 围成的曲边梯形的面积为 $f(t)-t^{2}$．(1) 求函数 $f(x)$；(2) 证明：当 $x>0$ 时，$f(x)>x^{2}+\dfrac{x^{3}}{3}$．
questions.explanation: (1) 由题意 $\int_{0}^{t}f(x)dx=f(t)-t^{2}$，两边对 $t$ 求导得 $f(t)=f'(t)-2t$，即 $f'(t)-f(t)=2t$；且当 $t=0$ 时面积为 $0$，得 $f(0)=0$。解一阶线性方程得 $f(t)=e^{t}\left(\int2te^{-t}dt+C\right)=e^{t}\left(-2te^{-t}-2e^{-t}+C\right)=Ce^{t}-2t-2$，由 $f(0)=0$ 得 $C=2$，故 $f(x)=2\left(e^{x}-x-1\right)\ (x\geq0)$。(2) 令 $F(x)=f(x)-x^{2}-\dfrac{x^{3}}{3}$，则 $F'(x)=2\left(e^{x}-1\right)-2x-x^{2}$，$F''(x)=2e^{x}-2-2x=2\left(e^{x}-x-1\right)=f(x)>0\ (x>0)$。故 $F'(x)$ 在 $(0,+\infty)$ 内单调递增，$F'(x)>F'(0)=0$，从而 $F(x)$ 在 $(0,+\infty)$ 内单调递增，$F(x)>F(0)=0$，即当 $x>0$ 时 $f(x)>x^{2}+\dfrac{x^{3}}{3}$。
questions.source: 2013年广东省专插本高等数学真题
questions.answerText: (1) $f(x)=2\left(e^{x}-x-1\right)$；(2) 证明见解析

questions.stem: 已知 $\left(1+\frac{2}{x}\right)^x$ 是函数 $f(x)$ 在区间 $(0,+\infty)$ 内的一个原函数。(1) 求 $f(x)$；(2) 计算 $\int_1^{+\infty}f(2x)\,dx$。
questions.explanation: (1) $f(x)=\left[\left(1+\frac{2}{x}\right)^x\right]'$。令 $y=\left(1+\frac{2}{x}\right)^x=e^{x\ln(1+\frac{2}{x})}$，则 $y'=e^{x\ln(1+\frac{2}{x})}\left[\ln\left(1+\frac{2}{x}\right)+x\cdot\frac{1}{1+\frac{2}{x}}\cdot\left(-\frac{2}{x^2}\right)\right]=\left(1+\frac{2}{x}\right)^x\left[\ln\left(1+\frac{2}{x}\right)-\frac{2}{x+2}\right]$。(2) 令 $t=2x$，则 $\int_1^{+\infty}f(2x)dx=\frac{1}{2}\int_2^{+\infty}f(t)dt=\frac{1}{2}\left[\left(1+\frac{2}{t}\right)^t\right]_2^{+\infty}=\frac{1}{2}\left[\lim\limits_{t\to+\infty}\left(1+\frac{2}{t}\right)^t-4\right]=\frac{1}{2}(e^2-4)=\frac{e^2}{2}-2$。
questions.source: 2010年广东省专插本高等数学真题
questions.answerText: $f(x)=\left(1+\frac{2}{x}\right)^x\left[\ln\left(1+\frac{2}{x}\right)-\frac{2}{x+2}\right]$；$\int_1^{+\infty}f(2x)\,dx=\frac{e^2}{2}-2$

About 70 million Americans are trying to lose weight. That is almost 1 out of every 3 people in the United States.Some people go in diet. This means they eat less of certain foods, especially fats and sugars.

Other people exercise with special equipment, take diet pills, or even have surgery. Losing weight is hard work, and it can also cost a lot of money. So why do so many people in the United States want to lose weight?

passages.eng-2005-read-B:
Instead of being playthings, early kites were used for military purposes. Historical records say they were large in size; some were powerful enough to carry men up in the air to observe enemy movements, and others were used to scatter some information over hostile forces. During the Tang Dynasty (618 - 907) , people began to fix on kites some bamboo (竹子) strips which, when high in the air, would ring in the wind like a zheng (a traditional Chinese musical instrument) .

Since then, the popular Chinese name for the kite has become fengzheng. The kites made today in some places are fixed with silk strings or rubber bands to give out pleasant ringing in the wind. It was also believed, for instance, during the Qing Dynasty (1644 - 1911) , that flying a kite and then letting it go , apart from the pleasure in itself, might send off one’s bad luck and illness.

Consequently it would bring him bad luch if one should pick up a kite lost by other people, This may be regarded as superstition (迷 信) but may not be altogether without reason: think of the good it will do to a person, ill and depressed all the time, if he or she could go out into the fields and fresh air to fly a kite. Chinese kites fall into two major types: those with wings that can be taken apart and those with wings that are fixed. The former can be taken apart and packed in boxcs.

Easy to carry about, they make good presents. The second type refers to those with fixed structure; they fly better and higher, given a steady wind, Classified by designs and other standards, there are no less than 300 varieties, including human figures, fish , insects, birds, animals and written Chinese characters. In size, they range from 304 meters to only 30 centimeters across.
passages.eng-2005-read-C:
One of Britain’s few distinctive contributions to world culture may come to an end, according to a survey that suggests holiday postcards are more and more given up because of emails and instant messages in mobile phones. More than half of the 1000 holiday- makers interviewed said they had decided to send fewer cards, turning instead to their electronic rivals. A quarter of the respondents (受调查者) regard postcards as old-fashioned and slow to arrive, A further 14% admitted that thinking of something to fill the space was too challenging, compared with a call home.

Although officially invented by a Hungarian, Emanuel Herrmann, in 1869, the idea of illustrated cards was taken up with most enthusiasm in Victorian Britain, joining Gothic architecture and landscape gardening as fields for which the country was famous. “If the British postcard did disappear, we would lose for ever something of great importance to the nation, ” said Chris Mottershead of Thomson Holidays, which did the survey. He was backed by Marie Angelou of Sussex University , who has investigated the importance of sending and receiving postcards.

“Postcards are nothing like phone calls, instant messages and direct photo shots via the mobile, ” she said. “All these are useful, practical devices, but postcards offer something else, something additional that is not simply functional,but imaginative and personal.

They can create the real atmosphere of your holiday in a way that nothing else can do. They are also for more than a moment——with some people adding them to collections built up over years and years.”
passages.eng-2005-read-D:
Despite a cooling of the economy, high-technology companies are still crying out for skilled workers. The Information Technology Association of America projects that more than 800,000 technology jobs will go unfilled next year. The lack of qualified workers poses a huge threat to the U.

S. economy. The most commonly cited reason for this state of affairs is that the country’s agrarian-age (农村时代) education system fails to prepare students in the primary and secondary grades for the 21st century work.

Yet an inadequate and outmoded education system is only part of the problem. A less tangible (明确的) but equally powerful cause is an antique (过时的) classification system that divides the workforce into two camps: white-collar knowledge workers and blue-collar manual laborers. Blue-collar workers emerged in the United States during the Industrial Age as work moved from farms to factories.

White-collar office workers became a significant class in the twentieth century, outnumbering (多 于) the blue-collar workers by mid-century. Corporations increasingly require a new layer of knowledge worker: a highly skilled multi-disciplined talent , who combines the mind of the white-collar worker with a solid grounding in mathematics and science (physics, chemistry, and biology ) These “ gold-collar ” workers— —so named for their contributions to their companies and to the economy as well as for their personal earning ability——apply their knowledge to technology.

The gold-collar worker already exists in a wide range of jobs. The maintenance technician who tests and repairs aircraft systems at American Airlines; the network administrator who manages systems and network operations at Procter & Gamble（宝洁公司）; the engineering technologist who assists scientists at Sandia National Laboratories;and the advanced-manufacturing technician at Intel can all be regarded as gold-collar workers.

passages.eng-2006-read-A:
Shopping for clothes is not the same experience for a man as it is for a woman. A man goes shopping because he needs something. His purpose is settled and decided in advance.

He knows what he wants, and his objective is to find it and buy it; the price is a secondary consideration. All men simply walk into a shop and ask the assistant for what they want. If the shop has it in stock, the salesman promptly produces it, and the business of trying it on proceeds at once.

All being well, the deal can be and often is completed in less than five minutes, with hardly any chat and to everyone’s satisfaction. For a man, slight problems may begin when the shop does not have what he wants, or does not have exactly what he wants. In that case the salesman, as the name implies, tries to sell the customer something else-he offers the nearest he can to the article required.

No good salesman brings out such a substitute bluntly; he does so with skill and polish:“I know this jacket is not the style you want, sir , but would you like to try it for size. It happens to be the color you mentioned.”Few men have patience with this treatment, and the usual response is:“This is the right color and may be the right size, but I should be wasting my time and yours by trying it on.” Now how does a woman go about buying clothes?

In almost every respect she does so in the opposite way. Her shopping is not often based on need. She has never fully made up her mind what she wants, and she is only“having a look round”.

She is always open to persuasion; indeed she sets great store by what the saleswoman tells her, even by what companions tell her. She will try on any number of things. Uppermost in her mind is the thought of finding something that everyone thinks suits her.

Contrary to a lot of jokes, most women have an excellent sense of value when they buy clothes. They are always on the lookout for the unexpected bargain. Faced with a roomful of dresses, a woman may easily spend an hour going from one rail to another, to and fro, often retracing her steps, before selecting the dresses she wants to try on.

It is a laborious process, but apparently an enjoyable one. Most dress shops provide chairs for the waiting husbands.
passages.eng-2006-read-B:
As a medium of exchange, money permits the separation of exchange into the two distinct acts of buying and selling, without requiring the seller to purchase goods from the person who buys his products, or vice versa. Hence producers who know they will be paid in money, can concentrate on finding the most suitable outlet for their goods, while buyers who will pay in money, can concentrate on finding cheapest market for the things they wish to purchase. Specialization, which is vital to an advanced economy, is encouraged, because people whose output is not a complete product but only a part of one in which many others are involved can be paid an amount equivalent to their share of the product.

Another advantage of money is that it is a measure of value-that is, it serves as a unit in terms of which the relative values of different products can be expressed. In a barter economy it would be necessary to determine how many plates were worth one hundred weight of cotton, or how many pens should be exchanged for a ton of coal, which would be a difficult and time-consuming task. The process of establishing relative values would have to be undertaken for every act of exchange, according to what products were being offered against one another, and according to the two parties’ desires and preferences.

If I am trying to barter fish bananas, for example, a lot would depend on whether the person willing to barter fish for bananas, for example, a lot would depend on whether the person willing to exchange bananas is or not keen on fish. Thirdly, money acts as a store of wealth. It is difficult to imagine saving under a barter system.

No one engaged on only one stage in the manufacture of a person could save part of his output, since he would be producing nothing complete. Even when a person actually produced a complete product the difficulties would be overwhelming.

Most products deteriorate fairly rapidly, either physically or in value, as a result of long storage; even if storage were possible, the practice of storing products for years on would involve obvious disadvantages-imagine a coal-miner attempting to save enough coal, which of course is his product, to keep him for life. If wealth could not be saved, or only with great difficulty, future needs could not be provided for, or capital accumulated to raise productivity.
passages.eng-2006-read-C:
Talk to those people who first saw films when they were silent, and they will tell you the experience was magic. The silent film had extraordinary powers to draw members of an audience into the story, and an equally potent capacity of make their imaginations work. It required the audience to become engaged-to supply voices and sound effects.

The audience was the final, creative contributor to the process of making a film. The finest films of the silent era depended on two elements that we can seldom provide today-a large and receptive audience and a well-orchestrated score. For the audience, the fusion of picture and live music added up to more than the sum of the respective parts.

The one word that sums up the attitude of the silent filmmakers is enthusiasm, conveyed most strongly before formulas took shape and when there was more room for experimentaion. This enthusiastic uncertainty often resulted in such accidental discoveries as new camera or editing techniques. Some films experimented with players; the 1915 film Regeneration, for example, by using real gangsters and streetwalkers, provided startling local color.

Other films, particularly those of Thomas Ince, provided tragic endings as often as films by other companies supplied happy ones. Unfortunately, the vast majority of silent films survive today in inferior prints that no longer reflect the care that the original technicians put into them. The modern versions of silent films may appear jerky and flickery, but the vast picture palaces did not attract four to six thousand people a night by giving them eyestrain.

A silent film depends on its visuals; as soon as you degrade those, you lose elements that go far beyond the image on the surface. The acting in silents was often very subtle and very restrained, despite legends to the contrary.
passages.eng-2006-read-D:
People have wondered for a long time how their personalities and behaviors are formed. It is not easy to explain why one person is intelligent and another is not, or why one is cooperative and another is competitive. Social scientists are, of course, extremely interested in these types of questions.

They want to explain why we possess certain characteristics and exhibit certain behaviors. There are no clear answers yet, but two distinct schools of thought on the matter have developed. As one might expect, the two approaches are very different from one another, and there is a great deal of debate between proponents of each theory.

The controversy is often referred to as“nature/nurture”. Two who support the“nature”side of the conflict believe that our personalities and behavior patterns are largely determined by biological and genetic factors. That our environment has little, if anything, to do with our abilities, characteristics, and behavior is central to this theory .

Taken to an extreme, this theory maintains that our behavior is predetermined to such a degree that we are almost completely governed by our instincts. Proponents of the “nurture”theory, or as they are often called, behaviorists, claimed that our environment is more important than our biologically based instincts in determining how we will act. A behaviorist, B.

F. Skinner, sees humans as beings whose behavior is almost completely shaped by their surroundings. The behaviorists’ view of the human being is quite mechanistic; they maintain that, like machines, humans respond to environmental stimuli as the basis of their behavior.

Neither of these theories can yet fully explain human behavior. In fact, it is quite likely that the key to our behavior lies somewhere between these two extremes. That the controversy will continue for a long time is certain.

passages.eng-2007-read-A:
In every school there is a “top” crowd that sets the pace, while the others follow their example. Let’s say the top crowd decides that it is smart to wear bright red sweaters （毛衣）. Pretty soon everybody is wearing bright red sweaters.

There is nothing wrong with that, except the fact that for some people bright red is rather unsuitable. The situation can even become dangerous, if the top crowd decides that it is smart to drink or drive cars at seventy miles an hour. Then the people who follow the example are putting their lives in danger.

They are like sheep being led to the slaughter （屠宰）. Now, it is likely that you have come across situations like these more than once in your life. In fact, it is likely that at one time or another you probably did something you knew to be wrong.

You may have excused yourself by saying, “Gee, the crowd does it.” Well, let the crowd do it, but don’t do it yourself. Learn to say “No.” Develop your own standards and your own judgments.

If you know the crowd is planning something of which you disapprove, have the courage to bow out gracefully. You’ll have the satisfaction of standing on your own two feet.
passages.eng-2007-read-B:
The fact that everybody enjoys a good mystery explains why magicians are such popular entertainers. We all know that a magician does not really depend on “magic” to perform his tricks, but on his ability to act at great speed. However, this does not prevent us from enjoying watching a magician produce rabbits from a hat, swallow countless eggs, or saw（锯）his wife in two.

Probably the greatest magician of all time was Harry Houdini who died in 1926. His real name was Enrich Weiss, but he adopted the name “Houdini” after reading a book which influenced him greatly. This had been written by a famous magician called Robert Houdini.

Houdini mastered the art of escaping. He could free himself from the tightest knots （最牢固的结）or the most difficult locks in seconds. Although no one really knows how he did this, there is no doubt that he had made a close study of every type of lock ever invented.

He would carry a small steel needle-like tool fastened to his leg and he used this instead of a key. Houdini once asked the Chicago police to lock him in prison. They bound him in chains and locked him up, but he freed himself in an instant.

The police accused him of having used a tool and locked him up again. This time he wore no clothes and there were chains round his neck, waist, wrists（手腕）,and legs; but he again escaped in a few minutes. Houdini had probably hidden his “needle” in a wax-like substance and dropped it on the floor in the passage（过道）.As he went past, he stepped on it so that it so that it stuck to （粘在）the bottom of his foot.

His most famous escape, however, was altogether astonishing. He was heavily chained up and shut in an empty wooden box the lid of which was nailed down. The box was dropped into the sea in New York harbor.

In one minute Houdini had swum to the surface. When the box was brought up, it was opened and the chains were found inside.
passages.eng-2007-read-C:
I lose so many things that I was sure they just get up and walk. Perhaps I have never admitted it—even to myself, but I am extremely jealous of people who are so orderly that they never lose anything. Most of my friends always seem to have a place for everything and everything is in its place.

I hate comparing myself with them. They have special cupboards for tools, hooks to hang things on and drawers to put things in . It is quite impossible for me to compete.

Some things have a terrible habit of disappearing the moment I need them. Pencils and ballpoint pens are never anywhere near the telephone when it rings, no matter how much care I take. Screw-drivers and tin-openers always manage to walk into the garden and, as a result, screws remain loose, and tins remain unopened.

Boxes of matches move under the radio, and needles disappear every time I want to sew a button on a shirt. The situation was getting so much out of control that I decided to organize myself. I had a large cupboard put into the kitchen.

On the shelves I neatly arranged a number of boxes and tins, the contents of which I clearly printed in ink on the outside. I had one box for pins, another for nails, and a special place for screw-drivers. There was a new address book in one corner so that I could make a note of telephone numbers and addresses.

Before this I had always written addresses on bits of paper——which I quickly lost. Soon everything was tidily arranged in its place, from pairs of scissors to cakes of soap and spare lamps. Having made such a sincere attempt to prevent things from running away, I felt very proud of myself.

But it was not long before the matches disappeared and the hammer decided to hide itself in the waste-paper basket. I soon got my revenge, however.

I had a lock fitted to the cupboard and thus made sure that nothing could escape. This was an admirable solution——until I lost the key to the cupboard.
passages.eng-2007-read-D:
While the history of technology can be traced along many lines, one of the most intriguing （引人入胜 的） development is that photo technology, the technology of light. From the prehistoric invention of fire to laser beams （激光束） and fiber optics （光纤）, light has “continually occupied the minds of inventors.” Their inventions fall into two groups: the use of light to aid vision and, more interestingly, the use of light for purposes of communication.

The use of light for communication is one of the major directions that technology has taken ever since the middle of the nineteenth century. From still （静态的）photography to movies to television (with a development from black-and-white to color imagery in each), photo technology has had a great effect upon mass communication and mass education. Unlike the printed word, visual images have more impact because they are more immediate: They copy reality in a way that the printed word cannot.

Unlike letter shapes, they are not abstract; unlike words, they require no symbolic interpretation by the mind. Combined with the widespread and uniform spreading of such images, phototechnology affects the thinking of vast audiences and shapes their view of reality. As the number of commercially available television channels grows, the viewer’s freedom of choice increases, but so does the burden of that choice.

passages.eng-2008-read-A:
In Western countries people have been using the installment（分期付款）plan since the first half of the twentieth century. Today, a large number of families in Great Britain buy furniture, household goods and cars by installment. In the U.S. , the figure is much higher than in Great Britain, and people there spend over 10 percent of their income on the installment plan.

The price of an article bought on installment is always higher than the price that would be paid by cash. There is a charge for interest. The buyer pays one quarter or one third of the price as a down payment（首期付 款）when the goods are delivered to him.

He then makes regular payments, weekly or monthly, until the full piece is paid up. The legal ownership of the goods remains with the seller until the final payment has been made. Installment buying has advantages and disadvantages.

It can help couples with small incomes to furnish their homes and start housekeeping. It increases the demand for goods, and in this way helps business and employment. There is, however, the danger that when business is bad, installment buying may end suddenly, making business much worse.

This may result in a great increase in unemployment. If the people on the installment plan lose their jobs, they will probably not be able to make their payments. If great numbers of people are not able to pay their installment debts there is a possibility that businessmen cannot collect their debts and will therefore lose money.

If businessmen lose money or fail to make a satisfactory profit, it becomes more likely to have a depression. This is why, in some countries, the government controls the installment plan by fixing the amount of the down payment and each of the following installments to discourage people from buying more than they can pay for on the installment plan.
passages.eng-2008-read-B:
Publicity（宣传，报道）offers several benefits. There are no costs for message time or space. An ad in prime time television may cost $ 250,000 or mare per minute, whereas a five-minute report on a network newscast would not cost anything.

However, there are costs for news releases （发布）, a publicity department, and other items. As with advertising, publicity reaches a mass audience. Within a short time, new products or company policies are widely known.

Credibility（可信度）about messages is high, because they are reported in independent media. A newspaper review of a movie has more believability than an ad in the same paper, because the reader associates independence with objectivity. Similarly, people are more likely to pay attention to news reports than ads.

Readers spend time reading the stories, but they flip through （草草翻阅）the ads. Furthermore, there may be hundreds of ads in a magazine. Feature stories （专题报道）are much fewer in number and stand out clearly.

Publicity also has some significant limitations. A firm has little control over messages, their timing, placement（报道顺序）, or coverage. It may issue detailed news releases and find only small portions of them reported by the media; and media have the ability to be much more critical than a company would like.

A firm may want publicity during certain periods, such as when a new product is introduced or new store opened, but the media may not cover the introduction or opening until after the time it would aid the firm. Similarly, media determine the placement of a story; it may follow a report on crime or sports.

Finally, the media ascertain（确定）whether to cover a story at all and the amount of coverage to be devoted to it. A company-sponsored（赞助）job program might go unreported or receive three-sentence coverage in a local newspaper.
passages.eng-2008-read-C:
The idea behind “ the rule of law ” is that it is laws based on logical reasons and clear thinking that should govern social life. “ We live under a rule of law, not of men. ” American teachers tell their students.

The students accept the idea. They believe that “no man is above the law,” and that laws apply equally to all people no matter how wealthy they are, what their personal connections are, or what their stations in life are. Their faith in the rule of law explains the belief many Americans held, and many foreigners could not understand, that President Richard Nixon should be removed from office as a result of his behavior in connection with what was called“ Watergate Scandal (水门事件)”.

Nixon had broken the law and therefore should be punished, Americans believed, even if he was the President. The belief in the rule of law goes beyond the area of politics to other areas of life that are governed by formal rules and procedures. To get a job with government institutions, for example, or to get government funding for a research project, one must follow published procedures and show that one meets the published requirements.

Personal connections are not supposed to matter under the rule of law. This is not to say that personal contacts, wealth, and social influence do not matter in situations where laws and rules are to be obeyed. They may.

What is said above describes the ideal with which Americans agree. In reality, connections can sometimes help a person get a government job.

Rich people can sometimes go unpunished for illegal behavior that poor people would be likely to be punished for. But in general the rule of law prevails, and Americans are proud that it does.
passages.eng-2008-read-D:
Human cloning（克隆） technology could be used to reverse heart attacks. Scientists believe that they may be able to treat heart attack victims by cloning their healthy heart cells and injecting them into the areas of the heart that have been damaged, and other problems may be solved if human cloning and its technology are not forbidden. With cloning, infertile couples could have children.

Current treatments for infertility, in terms of percentages（百分比）, are not very successful. Couples go through physically and emotionally painful procedures for a small chance of having children. Many couples run out of time and money without successfully having children.

Human cloning could make it possible for many more infertile couples to have children than ever before. We should be able to clone the bone marrow (骨髓) for children and adults suffering from leukemia (白血病). This is expected to be one of the first benefits to come from cloning technology.

We may learn how to switch cells on and off through cloning and thus be able to cure cancer. Cloning technology can be used to test for and perhaps cure gene-related diseases.

The above are just a few examples of what human cloning technology can do for mankind. This new technology promises unprecedented advancement in medicine if people will release their fears and let the benefits begin.

passages.eng-2009-read-A:
Once it was considered good to keep the car engine idling a minute or two following cold starts. Today, with modern technology, the opposite is true. An engine operating under road conditions will warm up faster and nun more efficiently than the one that is idling.

Idling just burns gas (on average, about a gallon an hour) . When you have a full tank of gas, park the car downhill. This will prevent any gas from coming out of the tank.

Parking in areas of less or no sunlight helps prevent the gas from steaming that would occur if you parked in the hot sun. Your car will stay cooler, too, and that means less gas consuming work for the air conditioner once the engine is started. Stay away from wide-track tires if you want top mileage (汽车耗费1 加仑油所行驶的路程)。 Narrow-track tires produce less friction and thus less rolling resistance.

The same effect is achieved by adding three to five pounds above recommended pressure to each tire; while this won't noticeably affect your car's sliding quality, it will increase tire life and gas mileage. Check tire pressure often, especially when the weather turns cold.

The difference between winter and summer tire pressure can be as much as eight pounds. This could cost you two miles per gallon.
passages.eng-2009-read-B:
A major incentive(动力)for college attendance is the belief that it will prepare you for a career. Chances are that the career you want, whether in nursing, counseling, law, or management, requires a college education. Even if the return of your education isn't as great as it used to be, you would probably rather he a relatively poorly paid lawyer than a secretary or a construction worker; you would probably rather be a manager than a managee.

In the sense that a degree is increasingly required for even middle-level jobs, your investment in a college education will still pay off. It can pay off in other ways too. It is a value judgment to say that a college education will make you a better person, but it is a value judgment that the vast majority of college graduates are willing to make.

Survey after survey demonstrates that people feel very positive about their college education, believing that it has made them better and more tolerant people. Whether it makes you a better person or not, a college education is likely to have a lasting effect on your knowledge and values. If you finish college， you will sit through 30 to 45 different courses.

Even the least dedicated student is bound to learn something from these courses. In addition, students learn informally. Whether you go to college in your hometown or across the country, college will introduce you to a greater diversity of people than you're likely to have experienced before.

This diversity will challenge your mind and broaden your horizons. As a result of formal and informal learning， college graduates are more knowledgeable about the world around them, more tolerant and less prejudiced， more active in public and community affairs, and, more open to mew ideas.
passages.eng-2009-read-C:
For the most part, rapid economic development has been a favor. But there is a down side to development -- health problems such as overweight are all becoming more common, as more people take taxis to work instead of riding their bicycles, and other labour-saving devices become more popular. An increasingly fast pace of life makes it difficult for people to spend time playing sports.

“I know exercise is good for your health,” a young lady said. “ But after a busy work week, the only thing I want to do is watch some TV and go to sleep.” That attitude may explain the results of a recent nationwide study, which suggested 15 percent of urban adults in China have heart problems.

Local researchers found that 31. 2 percent of elderly respondents (受访者) were getting enough exercise, but less than 9 percent of youngsters and the middle-aged got enough physical activity. Elderly people understand the importance of protecting their health.

The young people, however, are busy working and use this as an excuse to avoid exercise. In fact, physica1 exercise doesn't require much time, money or a special gymnasium. People can make use of any time and any place at their convenience to take part in sports.

Walking quickly, cycling, climbing the stairs and dancing are all helpful methods to improve one's health. The benefits of adding a little more activity to your life are priceless.

“There is no need to be an athlete(运动员)， however ，”a local doctor said. People should walk for 30 minutes a day and take part in some other physical activity three to five times a week ． He warns ， however ， that people in poor physical shape should start slowly ， and build up over time.
passages.eng-2009-read-D:
When he was young, Jacob Lawrence often walked more than sixty blocks from his home in the Harlem section of New York City to the Metropolitan Museum of Art. Jacob wanted to be an artist, and he believed that studying the famous painting hanging in that museum would help him. The year was 1930.

The depression (经济萧条) had brought hard times. As he walked through Harlem, Jacob noticed the people on the sidewalks. He looked hard at the churches, the funeral parlors and barbershops.

Jacob stored those images in his mind, along with the images of paintings he saw in the museum. Jacob came from a poor family. His mother believed there was little chance that her son could grow up to be a successful painter.

She wanted him to aim for something more practical. But Jacob's teacher in an after-school art program saw that the youngster was talented. Alston showed him how to use poster paints and crayons (蜡笔) to make masks and stage sets.

As time passed, Alston let Jacob rent work space in his own studio. That was an exciting place for a young black man struggling to become an artist. Many creative people gathered there to talk about art and literature and history.

From these conversations, Jacob learned that history books often ignored the accomplishments of African Americans. He decided to paint a series of pictures dramatizing the story of a black hero. He chose Toussaint, a slave from the Caribbean island of Haiti, who had helped free his people from French ruling.

Many people admired Jacob's pictures, but he needed more than admiration. To help his family, he often had to work at jobs that took him away from painting. Then something encouraging happened.

The government set up the Federal Art Project to help struggling artists survive the depression, and a sculptor (雕 刻家) named Augusta got Jacob a job with the project.For eighteen months, Jacob was paid a salary to paint pictures. For the first time, he felt like aprofessional artist.
